steps.title: Calculate one reference-cut force
steps.explanation: Use authored reference area 80 mm² and nominal stress 300 kPa. Their product is 24 N along the fibres. At zero pennation all of that force acts along the tendon direction.
steps.observe: Reference and current-cut forces both read 24 N. This is analytic bookkeeping with prescribed stress, not measured muscle strength.

steps.title: Change area and stress together
steps.explanation: Shorten to stretch 0.8 while imposing J=1. Current fibre-normal area becomes 80/0.8 = 100 mm² and Cauchy stress becomes 300 × 0.8 = 240 kPa.
steps.observe: 100 mm² × 240 kPa still gives 24 N. Shortening alone does not change the prescribed nominal force in this example.

steps.title: Project the force once
steps.explanation: Keep the same material cut and turn the fibres to 30 degrees. Tendon-directed force is the fibre force times cos(30 degrees).
steps.observe: Axial and current-cut forces stay 24 N; tendon-directed force becomes about 20.7846 N. Seven drawn lines encode orientation, not a fibre count.

steps.title: Check a familiar angle
steps.explanation: At 60 degrees the projection factor is one half. Projecting both an already projected area and the force again would apply the angle twice.
steps.observe: Tendon-directed force is 12 N while axial force remains 24 N. The orange cut slab is a diagram; the reported area is analytic.

audit.finding: The adapter lacked the stress readout needed to explain why changing current area did not change force.
audit.change: Report current Cauchy stress and reference area, then work through configuration matching and one pennation projection.
audit.remaining: Authored homogeneous bookkeeping. No source-bound fibre distribution, measured specific tension, force–length calibration or repaired anatomical equilibrium.
